subject: Post-call: POC scope, SLA tradeoffs, and benchmarking next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodai.com>
To: Lina Martin <lina.martin@avacarehealth.com>
Cc: Daniel Hopkins <daniel.hopkins@amazon.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Thanks — POC scope & immediate clarifying questions

Hi Lina — thanks again for the call today. Appreciate the clear descri ption of AvaCare's inference needs for clinical triage (burstiness during daytime hours, strict 99th pct latency targets for triage flows, and data residency constraints). Quick summary and asks so we can get the POC scoped and scheduled:

- Proposed POC goals (draft):
  • Verify 99th percentile latency ≤ 250ms at 512 tokens for production traffic profile.
  • Validate sustained throughput for peak hourly bursts (approx 120 qps).
  • Exercise graceful degradation path: failover to a quantized/cheaper model variant under capacity pressure.
  • Confirm KV/prefix caching effectiveness for repeated patient-context prompts.

- Technical clarifiers we need from your SRE:
  1) Will the POC use live PHI or de-identified test records? (affects security configs)
  2) Target window for the sustained-throughput test and preferred time zone for support engineers.
  3) Any mandatory egress/VPC endpoints we must use for Private deployment testing?

Next steps we recommend:
- We attach a draft POC_Scope_v1.pdf and a short benchmark matrix (Benchmark-matrix.xlsx) with proposed test cases.
- If you confirm goals above, we can provision a Dedicated trial pool (reserved capacity) and a hyperscaler-backed comparison (on-demand + reserved instance estimates) so you can see latency/cost tradeoffs side-by-side.

I'll loop in our sales lead Rishi and solutions engineer Lauren to coordinate timelines and the pricing/commitment questions. Can you confirm the SRE contact and whether we should use anonymized data for the tests?

Best,
Marcus
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
attachments: POC_Scope_v1.pdf (application/pdf), Benchmark-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Lina Martin <lina.martin@avacarehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@avacarehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks — POC scope & immediate clarifying questions

Thanks Marcus — great recap. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- We'll use de-identified records for the POC (we have a de-id pipeline).
- Our SRE lead Rajiv (cc'd) will own the test window scheduling. Rajiv — can you do the week of Nov 23 for a 2-day sustained throughput run?
- Data residency: tests must be run in us-west-2 and logs stored for 90 days; KMS is required.

I attached our procurement timeline and a short SRE checklist (Procurement-timeline.docx) — procurement wants to see commitment options and estimated monthly cost delta between a reserved capacity arrangement and hyperscaler reserved instances.

One question for Redwood: what's your fallback plan if Dedicated capacity saturates during the stress test? Do you have an automatic spillover to a cheaper variant or another region?

Best,
Lina
Head of Engineering, AvaCare Health
attachments: Procurement-timeline.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodai.com>
To: Lina Martin <lina.martin@avacarehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodai.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodai.com>, Daniel Hopkins <daniel.hopkins@amazon.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks — POC scope & immediate clarifying questions

Lina / Rajiv — thanks for the quick replies and for confirming de-id data + us-west-2 and KMS. Answers inline and a slightly refined test plan: 

- Fallback behavior: Redwood Dedicated can be configured with an automatic fallback policy that routes overflow to a compatible model variant (quantized or smaller transformer) or to a hosted on-demand pool in the same region. For the POC we recommend enabling both: 1) model-variant fallback with throttled token rate and 2) cross-pool spillover to a low-latency hosted pool if Dedicated saturates. We'll include both in the benchmark so you can observe quality vs cost tradeoffs.

- Refined test cases we'll run during the POC (proposed):
  1) Baseline single-request latency distribution (warm start).
  2) Sustained throughput run: 2 hours at ~120 qps, 50% of requests at 512 tokens.
  3) Burst test: 10-minute spike to 300 qps with concurrent cache-miss ratio.
  4) Failover simulation: intentionally reduce Dedicated pool to 60% capacity and observe routing/fallback behavior.
  5) Cost delta report: per-token/unit cost for Dedicated reserved vs hyperscaler reserved instances (estimated).

- Data/KMS/Residency: we can provision a Private control plane in us-west-2 and attach your KMS key for the POC; logs can be retained 90 days per your requirement.

Action items:
- Rajiv to confirm a final 2-day window (week of Nov 23 suggested).
- AvaCare to share SRE access (read-only) or a jumpbox for running distributed load drivers.
- Redwood to provide an initial billing delta estimate and SOW draft (2 business days after window confirmed).

Rishi / Lauren — can you prepare a short pricing note showing: 1) monthly cost for a 6-month reserved Dedicated pool sized for the POC peak, 2) a hyperscaler reserved instance alternative (monthly amortized), and 3) a runbook of fallback behaviors we will demonstrate?

Thanks — I will schedule a quick 30-min alignment next week to lock the details.

Cheers,
Marcus
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodai.com>
To: Lina Martin <lina.martin@avacarehealth.com>, Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@avacarehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodai.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodai.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:16:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks — POC scope & immediate clarifying questions

Hi Lina / Rajiv — quick pricing and procurement context from our side: 

- Reserved Dedicated: we offer monthly reserved pools with a minimum 3-month term (6-month committed pricing shown in the attached spreadsheet). Benefits: predictable unit costs, capacity isolation, and SLA-backed latency targets.
- Hyperscaler reserved instances: often lower sticker price for raw GPUs but carry hidden costs (network egress, model-ops overhead, kernel/stack tuning, and no Redwood routing/caching optimizations). Also less operational observability out of the box.

For procurement:
- If AvaCare needs a written estimate to compare against hyperscaler RI pricing, we can produce an itemized monthly delta (compute, networking, storage, Redwood Optimize discounts for batching/caching).
- On the SLA front: we can commit to a 99.9% uptime SLO for the Dedicated pool for production contracts; for the POC we provide elevated support hours and an operational readiness checklist but not the full SLA.

Question: does procurement need a sample contract clause for capacity guarantees or would a one-page commitment letter suffice for now?

Action: Marcus / Lauren — please draft the short one-page commitment letter + the itemized cost delta for the POC sizing Marcus specified. Lina / Rajiv — please confirm the preferred test dates (week of Nov 23) so we can lock hardware and SRE support.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@avacarehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodai.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodai.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodai.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks — POC scope & immediate clarifying questions

Thanks everyone — Nov 23–24 works for us for the 2-day run. A few operational notes from SRE: 

- We'll provide a read-only jumpbox and a KMS key with limited access.
- We'll expect Redwood engineers on-call during the runs (we can allocate a 4-hour overlap each day).
- Please include a short SOW (1 page) and estimated billing delta before Nov 20 so procurement can review.

Link to our SRE playbook and test harness: https://drive.avacare.com/sre/playbook (please treat as internal).

Also, procurement asked for a simple capacity-commitment clause example — a one-page commitment letter is fine for now. If the POC shows strong results, we'll escalate to procurement for a 12-month reserved capacity conversation.

I'll wait for the SOW and cost delta.

Rajiv
Senior SRE, AvaCare Health
